turns.question: Why did node inserts under a unique constraint get so slow in 6.0.0, and who fixed it?
turns.text:
**Cause:** In 6.0.0, UNIQUE enforcement scanned the whole label once per written entity. `check_node_constraint` in `graph/src/runtime/pending.rs` rebuilt a hash of every key in the label for each entity a commit touched, so a commit cost O(written × label size) and bulk inserts became quadratic. The issue's repro showed 20,000 nodes taking about 36 s on 6.0.0 versus about 0.3 s on 4.20.7 [1][2].

**Fix:** PR #3334, "enforce unique constraints by index lookup, not a label scan per entity," was authored by AviAvni and merged on 2026-10-14. It closes issue #3330 [3][4]. It looks each written entity up in the constraint's supporting index, compares written entities through a key set, and falls back to one label scan per commit when the index can't be used. The PR reports the repro's 10,001–20,000 range dropping from about 26 s to 20 ms [3].

**Related work:** PR #3225 by alblancc was closed unmerged [2][5], and PR #2997 by AviAvni is still open [5].

turns.question: Why did wrapping a WHERE predicate in parentheses stop the query from using the index?
turns.text:
The cause was a parenthesis wrapper that survived into the bound query tree, which hid the predicate from the optimizer.

- The parser keeps an `ExprIR::Paren` node for `( ... )`, which it needs for parsing. The binder copied that node into the bound tree. [1]
- The optimizer passes (`utilize_index`, `utilize_node_by_id`, filter push-down, Cartesian-to-hash-join) match on the filter root and on the children of a top-level `And`. A `Paren` node at those positions hid the predicate, so the index or id lookup was not applied. Results stayed correct; only the plan got worse. [1]
- Symptoms: on 6.0.0, `WHERE (n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1)` used a Node By Label Scan instead of a Node By Index Scan, and `WHERE (id(n) = 42)` fell back to All Node Scan + Filter instead of NodeByIdSeek. [2][3]

The fix (PR #3335, merged) works in the binder: it drops the `Paren` wrapper, since the tree shape already carries grouping, and it merges nested `And`/`Or` into a parent of the same operator. No optimizer pass has to know about parentheses. It closes issues #3331 and #3187. [1]</answer>

turns.text:
The cause was a parser artifact that leaked into the bound query plan. The parser keeps an `ExprIR::Paren` node for each `( ... )`, which it needs during parsing. The binder copied that node into the bound expression tree, and the optimizer passes that pick index and id lookups (`utilize_index`, `utilize_node_by_id`, filter push-down, Cartesian-to-hash-join) match on the filter's root and on the children of a top-level `And`. A `Paren` wrapper hid the predicate from those matches, so the planner fell back to a label scan or an all-node scan with a filter [1]. Results stayed correct; only the plan got slower. For example, on 6.0.0 `WHERE (n.k = 7 AND n.s = 1)` used a Node By Label Scan, while the unparenthesized form used a Node By Index Scan [2]. The parenthesized `id(n) = 42` case similarly lost NodeByIdSeek [3].

The fix, merged in PR #3335, drops the `Paren` wrapper in the binder, so `(x)` binds to the same IR as `x`. It also merges nested `AND`/`OR` into a parent of the same operator, so `(a AND b) AND c` splits into all three conjuncts. Because this is done once in the binder, no optimizer pass has to handle parentheses [4].</answer>

The slowdown was a quadratic cost in the uniqueness check. In 6.0.0, inserts into a label with a UNIQUE constraint were 35–120x slower than in 4.20.7, and the cost per node grew with the number of nodes already in the label [1].

Written entities are compared through a key set, and the label is scanned at most once per commit when the index can't match a value exactly. In the issue's repro, 10,001–20,000 nodes went from about 26 s to about 20 ms, and single CREATEs at 20k nodes dropped from about 2.9 ms to about 81 µs p50 [2].
